templates.pattern: An object moves in a circle of radius [R] m at a speed of [V] m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration?
templates.explanation: Centripetal acceleration a = v² ÷ r = [V]² ÷ [R] = [V*V] ÷ [R] = [RESULT] m/s²

templates.pattern: A [M] kg object moves in a circle of radius [R] m at [V] m/s. What is the centripetal force acting on it?
templates.explanation: Centripetal force F = mv² ÷ r = [M]×[V]² ÷ [R] = [M]×[V*V] ÷ [R] = [RESULT] N

templates.pattern: A projectile is launched horizontally at [U] m/s from a height of [H] m. How long does it take to reach the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
templates.explanation: Vertical: H = ½gt² → t = √(2H÷g) = √(2×[H]÷10) = √[2*H/10] = [RESULT] s. Horizontal speed does not affect fall time.

templates.pattern: A projectile is launched horizontally at [U] m/s from a height of [H] m. What horizontal distance does it cover before hitting the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
templates.explanation: Time of flight t = √(2H÷g) = √[2*H/10] s. Range = U×t = [U] × [RESULT] m

templates.pattern: A [M] kg object moving at [U] m/s collides elastically with an identical stationary object. What is the velocity of the first object after collision?
templates.explanation: In a perfectly elastic collision between equal masses where one is stationary, the moving object stops completely (velocity = 0 m/s) and the stationary one moves at [U] m/s.

templates.pattern: An object of mass [M1] kg moving at [U] m/s collides with a [M2] kg stationary object and bounces back. After collision, the [M2] kg object moves at [V2] m/s. What is the velocity of the [M1] kg object after collision?
templates.explanation: Conservation of momentum: m₁u = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ → v₁ = (m₁u − m₂v₂) ÷ m₁ = ([M1*U] − [M2*V2]) ÷ [M1] = [RESULT] m/s

templates.pattern: An object of mass [M] kg is attached to a string of length [R] m and swings in a vertical circle. What is the minimum speed at the top of the circle to maintain tension? (g = 10 m/s²)
templates.explanation: At minimum speed, tension = 0. mg = mv²÷r → v = √(gr) = √(10×[R]) = √[10*R] = [RESULT] m/s

templates.pattern: A rocket of mass [M] kg ejects gas at [VE] m/s. If it ejects [DM] kg of gas in 1 second, what is the thrust force produced?
templates.explanation: Thrust = exhaust velocity × mass flow rate = [VE] × [DM] = [RESULT] N. This is Newton's Third Law in action.

templates.pattern: An object of mass [M] kg falls from rest and reaches a terminal velocity of [VT] m/s. What is the drag force at terminal velocity? (g = 10 m/s²)
templates.explanation: At terminal velocity, drag force = weight = mg = [M] × 10 = [RESULT] N. Net force is zero so acceleration is zero.

templates.pattern: A [M] kg object is moving at [V] m/s. A constant force reduces its speed to [V2] m/s over [S] m. What is the magnitude of the force?
templates.explanation: Work-energy theorem: F×s = ½m(v²−v₂²) → F = m(v²−v₂²) ÷ 2s = [M]×([V*V]−[V2*V2]) ÷ (2×[S]) = [RESULT] N
